title: Your own fact checker

hero.alt: A fact-check report: each claim from a book chapter with a verdict, what was found, and the source

byline: A skill by CASBS alum John Markoff
intro: Working on your book? This skill checks every number, date, name and quote in a chapter and shows its sources. It flags, it never rewrites. About 20 minutes.

steps.title: Put it with your writing
steps.body: Drag SKILL.md into the folder with your chapter. Word, PDF and text files all work.

steps.title: Open the folder in Claude
steps.body: Code tab, new project, pick that folder. Trust the workspace.

steps.title: Hand Claude the skill
steps.say: There's a file called SKILL.md in this folder. It's a fact-checking skill. Set it up so I can use it any time, then fact-check chapter-3.docx.

steps.title: Start with the fact-check
steps.body: It can also copy edit, suggest plainer sentences, check the chapter against itself and give an editor's read. Click Allow when it asks to search the web.

steps.title: Read the report
steps.body: Saved next to your chapter as …_factcheck. Each claim: verified, partly accurate, inaccurate or could not be verified, with a source link.

steps.title: Check the checker
steps.body: Open a few of its sources, starting with anything marked inaccurate.
steps.trap: "Could not be verified" means look it up yourself.

next.title: Tomorrow
next.body: Same project: say "fact-check chapter 4". In Claude, rename and pin the project so you find it.
